quote: the gap in held-out reconstruction between $\vz$ and a one-hot type code

quote: the programmes it has switched on or off because of who its neighbours are
issue: The second component is defined causally ('because of', 'response'). But w also absorbs, by the paper's own design, intrinsic variation that is spatially organised within a type (method.tex:169: 'pushed into w, tumour subclones being the sharp case'), and cells that select or migrate into niches produce the same association. The sweep separates association from leakage only. A 2026-09-23 paperlog entry already removed the causal reading from the method ('Causal reading belongs in discussion only'), but the abstract and intro still carry it.
why: The core premise is that there are three components. A reviewer will point out that the model cannot separate the second from spatially organised intrinsic variation or from selection. The paper concedes this in §2.5 but not where the claim is made.
proposed_change: introduction.tex:4: "Second, its \emph{response} to the local microenvironment: the programmes it has switched on or off because of who its neighbours are ..." -> "Second, variation that goes with its local microenvironment, including the programmes it has switched on or off in response to its neighbours ..." Abstract: "a latent response $\vw$ to a deterministic description of its microenvironment" -> "a latent $\vw$ for the expression predicted by a deterministic description of its microenvironment". Add to method.tex:228 (or the intro's sweep sentence): "The sweep separates spatial association from leakage. It does not separate a response from intrinsic variation that is spatially organised within a type, which conditional invariance assigns to $\vw$, nor from cells selecting their niche. A surviving effect is an association that leakage cannot explain."

quote: A model that explains everything with leakage reconstructs held-out cells well
issue: With kappa fixed at most 0.4, the model cannot route 'everything' to leakage. This motivation belongs to a design where kappa was learned. The failure mode the guard actually targets is stated later in the same paragraph: invariance emptying z while reconstruction stays good.
why: A reviewer will note that the motivating failure cannot occur under the stated model.
proposed_change: Replace the sentence with "A model whose invariance machinery has emptied $\vz$ of type structure can still reconstruct held-out cells well through the response and the leakage mixture, so held-out reconstruction alone is not a valid stopping criterion."

quote: while an independent probe still finds the leak
issue: 'Leak' and 'leakage' mean two different things in the paper: transcript misassignment (κ, β, 'leakage sweep') and residual niche information in z. To ML readers, 'leakage' also means train/test information leakage, which the paper discusses too (held-out tiles in training rings). The ST literature calls the technical effect misassignment, spillover, admixture or contamination.
why: The invariance section and the leakage model are exactly the two mechanisms the paper says must not be merged, and the shared word blurs them.
proposed_change: Keep 'leakage' for transcripts only, with one defining clause in intro:4: "(\emph{leakage}; also called spillover or misassignment)". In the invariance section, write 'residual dependence' instead: method.tex:191 'an independent probe still finds residual dependence'.

issue: A single 466-word paragraph announces 'four statements' but never numbers them. They are: κ not identified; rotation plus per-column softmax constants; the per-type translation; and the z/w allocation. The gauge consequences and the iVAE/Locatello positioning are interleaved with them. The model's symmetries are its only formal content, yet they are asserted in prose, with no proposition or proof. quote: It is not the evidence lower bound of a single model, so $q$ is not the posterior of anything
issue: The appendix derives both L_i (l.9–12) and L_i^z (l.26) as lower bounds on the *same* log p(x_i | c_i, t_i). So L_i + ωL_i^z ≤ (1+ω) log p(x_i | c_i, t_i), a scaled bound on the evidence of one model. L^z is not a bound for "the model in which w is not inferred" (l.24 and method.tex:134). It is the same model with a restricted variational family, q(w) := p(w | c,t). What is true: q(z) is shared by two variational families, so its maximiser is a compromise and is not the best approximation to p(z|x) in either family. This differs from DisCoVR, where the shared-only bound belongs to a different model.
why: The "q is not a posterior, so uncertainty comes from the sweep" argument rests on this sentence. An ML reviewer can check in two lines that the sentence contradicts the derivation directly above it.
proposed_change: derivations.tex:30, replace the first two sentences with: "Both bounds are on the same evidence, so L_i + ωL_i^z ≤ (1+ω) log p(x_i | c_i, t_i). Unlike in \citet{slavutsky2025}, whose two bounds belong to different models, ours belong to two variational families of one model, q(z)q(w|z) and q(z)p(w|c,t), which share q(z). The shared factor is fitted to a compromise and is not the best approximation to p(z|x) within either family, which is one of the reasons uncertainty is reported from the leakage sweep rather than from q." In method.tex:134 and derivations.tex:24, replace "for the model in which w is not inferred" with "by restricting the variational family to q(w_i) := p(w_i | c_i, t_i)".
evidence: [TEXT] derivations.tex:9 "log p(x_i | c_i,t_i) = … ≥ …"; derivations.tex:26 "log p(x_i | c_i, t_i) ≥ … =: L_i^z"; derivations.tex:30 "It is not the evidence lower bound of a single model"; method.tex:159 "q is not the posterior of any single model even at the bound-equivalent weights" (can stay after the fix).

quote: At the depth of in situ data, tens to a few hundred counts over thousands of genes, gene-wise overdispersion cannot be estimated in any case
issue: (i) The depth claim is wrong for two of the four datasets: mean counts are 140 (GSE core), 262 (ovarian), 441 (lung) and 1,663 (ovary FF). (ii) "Cannot be estimated" is too strong. A per-gene dispersion is a population parameter estimated across 10^5–10^6 cells, and scVI does so routinely at comparable per-gene sparsity. The defensible point is that dispersion is confounded with a flexible latent and would break the exact mixture. (iii) The text makes the Dirichlet-multinomial conditional on overdispersion "at higher depth". The FF section is at higher depth, so that check is now owed.
why: The audit (A5) used this very sentence as the correct depth statement, but it is also off. Single-cell reviewers will challenge "cannot be estimated".
proposed_change: "At the depth of these data, from about a hundred to a few thousand counts per cell over thousands of panel genes, per-gene dispersions are estimable across cells but are confounded with a flexible latent, and a low-dimensional amortised $\vz$ absorbs much of what a dispersion parameter captures in coarser models. Should posterior predictive checks show overdispersion, as is most likely on the deepest section, the appropriate extension…" Leave the check itself for the evaluation.
evidence: [DATA] mean counts per cell: GSE core 140, ovarian 262, lung 441, ovary FF 1,663 (task facts; ovarian re-checked: mean 261.6, median 178 in full.h5ad). [MEM] scVI gene-wise NB dispersion.

quote: under it $\vz$ must explain the cell given only the \emph{expected} response
issue: This holds only at kappa = 0. The intrinsic path decodes cell i with a prior draw w-breve_i, but mixes in the same rhobar_i as the first term. That rhobar_i is built from the neighbours' posterior (realised) responses w_j. The paper itself says (:206) that neighbours share niches, so w_j ≈ w_i. So for kappa > 0, a fraction kappa of the realised local response reaches L_i^z through the leakage term. The tie-breaker towards z therefore weakens as kappa grows, and the z/w allocation it enforces changes along the grid for a reason other than leakage.
why: The sweep reads z- and w-side readouts as functions of kappa and attributes their movement to leakage. Some of that movement is a kappa-dependent change in the allocation mechanism itself. Reviewers checking why readouts move 'mechanically' (:228) will find this second mechanism unstated.
proposed_change: At :142, qualify the sentence: 'given only the expected response of the cell itself; the foreign influx still carries the neighbours' realised responses, so the pressure on z weakens as κ grows.' At :228, add it to the readouts expected to move with κ by construction.
